- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

content.content: 1 # Spec — meeting-room booking app (owner: supervisor, verbatim user requirements; FINAL, do not ask questions) 2 3 Constraints: Node.js built-ins only (no npm install). Node v22. Tests use node:test. Do not use the Fable model. 4 5 Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. 6 7 ## Server 8 - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. 9 - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. 10 - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. 11 - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. 12 - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. 13 - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. 14 - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. 15 - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. 16 - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. 17 - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. 18 19 ## API 20 - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. 21 - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. 22 - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. 23 - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. 24 - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. 25 - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. 26 - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. 27 - `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. When `` is not a positive integer written in ASCII digits 0-9 without a leading zero, or no booking has that id: 404 `booking not found`. 28 - `GET /` and `GET /app.js` serve the page (see Page). 29 - Any other path: 404 `not found`, whatever the method. This includes every path that starts with `/api/bookings/` and whose rest is empty or holds a `/`, such as `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/`. 30 - A path above with a method not listed for it (HEAD and OPTIONS included): 405 `method not allowed`. For example `GET /api/bookings/abc` is 405. A 405 reply may or may not have an `Allow` header; it is not checked. 31 - Every reply with a body other than the page and the script has `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. An error reply is `{"error": ""}` with exactly that key, where `` is the text given here. 32 33 ## Booking rules (`POST /api/bookings`; the first rule that fails decides the reply) 34 1. The media type of the `Content-Type` header (the part before the first `;`, with spaces and tabs removed from both ends, letter case ignored) is not `application/json`, or the header is missing: 415 `content type must be application/json`. 35 2. The body is longer than 10000 bytes, counting the body bytes actually received: 413 `body too large`. 36 3. The body, decoded as `Buffer.prototype.toString('utf8')` does and then given to `JSON.parse`, is not a JSON object (it is empty, not valid JSON, `null`, an array, a string, a number or a boolean): 400 `body must be a JSON object`. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 become U+FFFD and are not an error by themselves. A byte order mark at the very start is kept, so such a body is not valid JSON. 37 4. `room` is not a string equal to one of the room names (letter case matters): 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos`. 38 5. `title` is not a string, or is shorter than 1 or longer than 80 UTF-16 code units after removing the whitespace at both ends (as `String.prototype.trim` does): 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters`. The booking keeps the trimmed title. 39 6. `date` is not a string `YYYY-MM-DD` (4, 2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) naming a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31, where February has 29 days in years divisible by 4: 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. 40 7. `start` is not a string `HH:MM` (2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) from `00:00` to `23:59`: 400 `start must be HH:MM`. 41 8. `end` is not such a string: 400 `end must be HH:MM`. 42 9. `end` is not later than `start`: 400 `end must be after start`. 43 10. The booking overlaps a booking of the same room on the same date, that is each of the two starts before the other ends (a booking may start exactly when another ends): 409 `room is already booked from to `, with the start and end of the overlapping booking that starts earliest. 44 - No field except `title` is trimmed or changed: ` 2026-11-03`, `2026-11-3` and `9:00` are invalid. 45 46 ## Page 47 - `GET /` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8` and the page. `GET /app.js` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/javascript; charset=utf-8` and the page's script. 48 - The page loads the script with a `

1	# Decisions (supervisor)
2	
3	- File layout (project root): `server.mjs` (backend), `public/index.html` + `public/app.js` (frontend; server reads them from the folder of server.mjs via `new URL('./public/...', import.meta.url)`, at startup or per request — read failure = 500 `internal error`), `test/*.test.mjs` (testing), `package.json` (backend), `README.md` (docs).
4	- package.json: `{"type":"module","scripts":{"start":"node server.mjs","test":"node --test test/"}}` — no dependencies.
5	- Data file layout: `{"nextId": <int>, "bookings": [ {id,room,title,date,start,end}, ... ]}`. Validate fully on load (nextId positive integer > every id; each booking exact keys and valid fields); otherwise `cannot read data file <name>`.
6	- Saving: write to the data file (writeFile directly to the path; no folder creation). Serialize all mutations through one promise queue so concurrent POSTs behave sequentially. Apply in-memory change only after the write succeeded.
7	- Spec is in `.team/notes/spec.md` and is final. Where a line can be read two ways, take the stricter reading and note it here.
8	- 2026-11-03 · frontend · A rooms or list reply with status 200 whose body lacks the expected array (or a list entry that is not an object): `#error` shows `Request failed.`; the list is kept and `#room` stays empty. Why: spec is silent; never throw, never show guessed content.
9	- 2026-11-03 · frontend · GET requests pass `{ method: 'GET' }` explicitly; any reply with status 204 skips json() (only DELETE expects it; for GET/POST it is then an error status with `Request failed.`). Why: stricter reading of "a reply other than a 204 whose body cannot be read counts as no reply".
10	- 2026-11-03 · frontend · Book/Cancel re-enable runs in the request helper's `finally`, in the same tick fetch/json() settles, before the outcome is handled. Why: "enabled again as soon as the request settles, before anything else happens".
11	- 2026-11-03 · backend · Data file accepted only in the exact layout the server writes (exact keys, nextId > every id, unique ids, trimmed titles, no overlapping bookings); ENOTDIR (a file on the path) is not ENOENT, so it fails startup. Why: stricter reading of "not data in the layout this server writes" / "fails with ENOENT".
12	- 2026-11-03 · backend · Content-Type media type: ASCII-only lowercasing, trims only spaces/tabs (not String.trim). DELETE id compared as a string to stored ids, so huge ids never round onto an existing id. CONNECT is answered 404/405 on the raw socket. Why: stricter readings of rule 1, the delete id rule and "whatever the method".
13	- 2026-11-03 · testing · package.json test script is `node --test "test/**/*.test.mjs"`: on Node 22 `node --test test/` treats `test/` as a module and fails. Why: `npm test` must run every test file.
14	- 2026-11-03 · testing · Near-miss copies (`.team/near-miss/<n>-<file>`, built by `.team/tools/near-miss-make.mjs`) are swapped in and restored inside a scratch copy of the project in the OS temp folder (`.team/tools/near-miss-run.mjs`), never in the real tree. Why: other sections edit server.mjs in parallel; an in-place swap could overwrite their edits.
15	- 2026-11-03 · testing · Tests accept GET requests from app.js with no options or `method: 'GET'`; PORT failure stderr is checked as exactly one non-empty line with no stack trace (spec: "one line of its choice"). Why: spec leaves those free.

content.text:
I re-graded the testing section's suite and it **passes the gate**: overall 9/10, lowest item 8. `npm test` gives 414 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped. I re-ran six of the 41 near-miss copies (6, 14, 22, 39, 40 and 41) and the suite kills all six; the originals pass inside the scratch copy.

**Round-1 asks, checked one by one:**
- **Shared helpers:** done. `uniqueDate`, `withTemp`, `JSON_TYPE` and `expectError` are in `/root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/test/helpers/server.mjs`. `NO_REPLY`, `FAILED`, `methodOf`, `spyOnText` and `flush` are in `/root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/test/helpers/page.mjs`.
- **Page elements:** done. `page-script-api` now builds its fake elements from the real `public/index.html`.
- **Local fetch helpers:** `page-actions` has its own `hookedFetch` and `page-script-api` has its own `fire`. These are the small local needs you allowed around `fake-dom.mjs`.
- **Skips:** done. The 65535 and 3000 tests use `t.skip` and only swallow `EADDRINUSE`/`EACCES`. The port-3000 test still checks the failure path before it skips.
- **Request lists:** done. The undefined-status hack is replaced by `NON_MUTATING_BASE` plus `NON_MUTATING_FIXTURE_ONLY`.
- **Bad data files:** done. There are 36 cases, covering every type you listed, and a valid 3-booking file with nextId 10 as the positive control.
- **Save failures:** done. stdout and stderr are checked after the failed saves.
- **Unexpected failure:** done. The new test copies `server.mjs` without `public/`, gets 500 `internal error`, and the server keeps running.
- **Pipelined replies:** done. `splitResponses` splits them exactly by Content-Length.
- **Routing, refetch and Cancel:** done. The routing POST status is asserted and `methodOf` is used in refetch detection. Cancel has the bad-JSON 404 and the DELETE 200 tests, and a GET answered 204 counts as an error status.
- **Invisible characters:** only partly done. `'A�B'` at `request-body.test.mjs:211` is still a literal U+FFFD.

**Main gap:** no test catches a server that uses up an id on a rejected POST (400 or 409). The spec says "each new booking the next integer". The only id checks are `assert.notEqual(first, second)` at `booking-rules.test.mjs:213` and `assert.notEqual(json.id, 99)` at `:163`, and both pass against that bug.

**Coverage:** I did not measure it. `server.mjs` runs as a child process and `app.js` runs inside `vm`, so a coverage report would not count them.

## GRADE
Overall: 9/10
Verdict: pass
